thread:
maria_support: customer reported spikes in prod hitting 429s even though they have a Dedicated reserved pool
maria_support: customer_id=acme-42, reserved_pool=rp-7f3a, committed_qps=120, observed_429_start=2024-11-08T14:12:05Z
aj_oncall: thanks, sending initial repro link to logs. do we have recent pool headroom metrics?
aj_oncall: @peter_infra can you pull pool token-bucket traces for rp-7f3a around 14:00-14:30 UTC?
peter_infra: grabbing now, looks like token refill stayed at 120 qps but bursts pushed instantaneous demand to ~220 qps
peter_infra: snippet from pool debug (trimmed):
```
2024-11-08T14:09:58Z demand=98
2024-11-08T14:12:07Z demand=218 -> rate_limiter:emit 429 reserved_pool_capacity
2024-11-08T14:12:11Z demand=205 -> auth:ok
2024-11-08T14:12:30Z demand=130 -> allowed
```
maria_support: customer claims they saw sustained 3-4s latencies, then 429 flood for ~45s
ingrid_eng: if demand spikes > committed_qps and smoothing isn't configured, bursts can exhaust the pool fast. do we have their smoothing policy?
aj_oncall: their tenant config: smoothing: disabled, max_burst_window: 0, allow_burst: true (legacy)
maria_support: they migrated from hosted to Dedicated last month, maybe default smoothing didn't carry over
peter_infra: confirmed: migration path left allow_burst=true and no burst buffer. token bucket capacity = 1.5x qps by default but that was ignored for dedicated rp due to config bug (tracked earlier)
ingrid_eng: oh — we saw a bug in allocator that ignored pool_burst_buffer for rp created before 2024-09. need to check if rp-7f3a is old
peter_infra: rp-7f3a created 2023-12-05. that matches
maria_support: customer asking: why do we return 429 instead of queueing or failing to new lower-tier fallback model?
ingrid_eng: current policy: for Dedicated reserved pools we prefer strict quota enforcement to meet SLA for committed throughput. fallback routing only happens when global fallback policy is enabled or there's a compatible cheaper model pinned. in their case fallback isn't configured
aj_oncall: immediate mitigations for customer: 1) enable smoothing (recommended) 2) increase reserved pool commit or allow a short managed burst buffer 3) enable fallback->compatible smaller model
maria_support: they want repro steps so they can test with dev traffic. suggested minimal curl:
```
for i in $(seq 1 300); do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDDO_TOKEN" \
       -H "X-Reserved-Pool: rp-7f3a" \
       -d '{"input":"x"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
```
maria_support: run from a machine with parallelism 50 to reproduce local spike
aj_oncall: also check response headers, we add: X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-Reserved-Pool, X-Error-Details
maria_support: sample 429 response body they saw: `{ "error":"rate_limit_exceeded", "reason":"reserved_pool_capacity", "retry_after": 30 }`
billing_bot: note: if they increase reserved commit, billing throttle tier will change at next billing cycle — FYI
peter_infra: long-term fix: we need to patch allocator to honor legacy pool_burst_buffer during migration and auto-apply smoothing policy when allow_burst=true
ingrid_eng: quick patch idea: if rp.created_at < 2024-09 AND allow_burst=true AND smoothing unset -> set smoothing=filtered-exponential, burst_buffer=0.8*qps
aj_oncall: can we temporarily flip smoothing for this tenant now? who can push that change safely?
peter_infra: I can apply a tenant-level override for acme-42: set smoothing=on, burst_buffer=60 (50% of commit) — will apply in control plane in 5m
maria_support: customer agreed to try temporary smoothing. scheduling change window now
maria_support: post-change result: 14:18->14:26 saw no 429s, peak latency trimmed to ~700ms
aj_oncall: collect metrics from 14:10-14:30 and send to customer support with before/after graphs
ingrid_eng: follow-up: we should run a migration job to detect all pre-2024-09 pools and ensure burst buffer and smoothing are applied. file a Jira?
peter_infra: created INF-4821: "legacy reserved-pool migration: enforce burst buffer + smoothing". assigning to ingrid
maria_support: customer note: they'd prefer auto-fallback to a cheaper model rather than increasing commit for now — added to action items
aj_oncall: owner list: ingrid_eng (fix), peter_infra (temp overrides + migration job), maria_support (customer comms), billing_bot (quote if commit increases)
maria_support: closing note: quick triage steps for oncall
- check reserved_pool token traces
- inspect tenant smoothing config
- repro with parallel curl, capture response headers
- if legacy pool: apply temporary smoothing override
- file migration Jira

maria_support: tagging this resolved for now, will reopen if customer reports further 429s
